operations_plan.summary: Identify the Cyclops Plus Heatsink rear three-point mounting interface, resolve the Cyclops Aqua Block four-point reference, and derive the replacement hole pattern without altering geometry.

steps.description: Establish the model coordinate convention using the supplied semantic orientation, with +Y defined as the back. On the finned Cyclops Plus Heatsink, identify the broad rear planar mounting face of solid 1 by selecting the exterior planar face whose outward normal is parallel to +Y. Use geometric face filtering within F-02-02 rather than assuming a specific member of the supplied face range. Preserve the cooling-fin faces in F-02-03 and all other exterior envelope faces.

On the rear face identified in OP-01-S01, classify the existing three mounting points by tracing each opening through its coaxial cylindrical, threaded, chamfered, counterbored, and terminal faces. Select only the three smaller attachment holes visible as the triangular three-point pattern on the +Y rear view. Exclude the two large functional bores, hotend passages, and any side-oriented service ports. Record each selected hole's center in a local rear-face coordinate system, axis direction, diameter or thread geometry, counterbore or countersink geometry, depth, and termination condition.

Resolve the Cyclops Aqua Block reference component in the exploded model. Solid 0 in SEC-01 is the provisional Aqua Block candidate because it is the non-finned manifold-like body with repeated symmetric stepped feed and mounting bores. Confirm this identification from native component metadata or assembly naming before editing. On its +Y rear mounting face, isolate the four attachment-point bore chains associated with the rear mounting interface, using F-01-03 for stepped mounting bores and F-01-01 only if the relevant attachment points contain modeled threads. Do not treat large feed or fluid passages as mounting points. This is an unresolved reference if solid 0 cannot be confirmed as the Cyclops Aqua Block or if four mounting-only bores cannot be unambiguously isolated; in that case, require the native Aqua Block reference or a dimensioned four-hole pattern rather than guessing.

Construct a local 2D datum system on both confirmed rear faces. Set each datum origin from stable body references such as the midpoint between the two preserved large functional-bore axes and orient its axes using the heatsink side faces and top/bottom envelope. Transfer the four Aqua Block mounting centers into the heatsink rear-face datum while preserving their horizontal and vertical offsets, symmetry, and orientation relative to the functional-bore datum. Extract the complete source hole definition directly from the Aqua Block, including nominal bore size, thread specification where present, counterbore or countersink diameters, entry chamfers, depths, and termination conditions. No numerical parameters are stated in the request, so all such parameters must be measured or associatively referenced from the confirmed Aqua Block geometry.

Perform a pre-edit clearance and wall-thickness analysis for the four transferred axes. Intersect virtual cylinders representing the full source hole stacks with solid 1 and verify that they remain within the heatsink core, do not break into the two large functional bores or other internal passages, and do not cut the cooling fins, side holes, threaded service ports, or top-facing openings. Compare the four transferred holes with the existing three-point pattern and classify existing holes as reusable only when center, axis, hole type, size, and depth all match the Aqua Block definition within CAD tolerance. Mark all other old mounting holes as obsolete.

operations_plan.summary: Remove or heal the obsolete portions of the Cyclops Plus Heatsink three-point rear mounting pattern while retaining any fully compatible coincident mounting holes.

steps.description: If an editable feature history exists, locate and suppress only the hole, thread, counterbore, countersink, and chamfer features that generate the obsolete rear mounting points identified in OP-01-S05. Do not suppress shared features that also generate preserved side ports or functional passages. Retain any old mounting point classified as fully coincident and geometrically compatible with one of the four transferred Aqua Block points.

For an imported or history-free B-rep, delete the complete connected face chains of each obsolete mounting hole, including modeled thread flanks, roots, crests, runouts, cylindrical bore walls, annular shoulders, and entry chamfers. Reconstruct the removed material with bounded additive fills or direct face replacement up to the original exterior and internal limiting faces. Extend the surrounding rear planar face across each former opening and heal the result so that no residual annular edges, partial threads, or internal voids remain.

Validate the healed heatsink as a single watertight solid. Confirm that the rear face is planar at all removed-hole locations and that healing has not changed the fin stack, the outer body envelope, the two large rear functional bores, top openings, side ports, or internal passage connectivity. Save this healed state as the base body for the new mounting cuts.

operations_plan.summary: Create the four-point Cyclops Aqua Block-style mounting interface on the rear face of the Cyclops Plus Heatsink and verify preservation of all non-mounting geometry.

steps.description: Create or activate a sketch on the +Y rear planar face of solid 1. Project the stable datum references established in OP-01-S04, including the two preserved large functional-bore axes and appropriate body centerlines. Place four construction points at the transferred Aqua Block mounting coordinates. Fully constrain the points using the extracted horizontal and vertical offsets, symmetry relations, and datum alignment; do not infer dimensions from image scale.

At each of the four constrained points, create the principal mounting bore normal to the rear face and directed into the heatsink body. Reproduce the confirmed Aqua Block bore diameter and termination type exactly, such as blind to a measured depth or through-all only when the source mounting point is through-all. If an existing compatible hole was retained, reference it as one of the four points instead of recutting it.

Apply the source mounting-hole secondary geometry to all four points. Where the Aqua Block uses internal threads, reproduce the same thread specification, handedness, pitch, threaded length, entry relief, and runout; use modeled helical threads if the source uses modeled threads. Where it uses counterbores, countersinks, annular seats, or entry chamfers, reproduce their measured diameters, angles, and depths in the same axial order. Maintain four identical hole stacks unless the confirmed Aqua Block reference explicitly contains differing hole definitions.

Regenerate the model and inspect the rear interface from +Y. Verify that exactly four mounting points are present in the transferred Aqua Block arrangement and that no obsolete third-point opening or partial hole geometry remains. Check center positions, axes, diameters, thread or counterbore definitions, and depths against the source geometry using a face-to-face or feature measurement comparison.

Run final topology, interference, and preservation checks. Confirm solid 1 remains watertight and that every new mounting hole has adequate surrounding wall material and no intersection with large bores or internal passages. Compare the final heatsink against the pre-edit body outside the local rear mounting regions and require zero geometric change to F-02-03 cooling fins, the external body envelope, large functional bores, top-facing openings, side holes, non-mounting threads, counterbores, chamfers, and all hotend alignment interfaces. Confirm that solid 0 and all other solids remain unchanged.
